models.method_details: The authors report OLS coefficient estimates.

dependent_variable.name: Ln(Liquidity Factor + 1)
dependent_variable.definition: Natural logarithm of one plus the score of the first and only factor with eigenvalue greater than one, extracted by factor analysis from four quarterly liquidity proxies: the median quoted bid-ask spread; the share of trading days with zero returns; the median Amihud price-impact measure (daily absolute stock return divided by U.S.-dollar trading volume, omitting zero-return days); and estimated total round-trip trading costs (bid-ask spreads, commissions, and implicit costs such as short-sale constraints or taxes).

evidence.quote: the Liquidity Factor equal to the factor scores extracted from the four individual measures bid-ask spreads, zero returns, price impact, and total trading costs using factor analysis
the factor scores from the first (and only) factor with an Eigenvalue greater than one as dependent variable
Zero Returns is the proportion of trading days with zero daily stock returns out of all potential trading days in a given quarter.
Price Impact is the quarterly median of the Amihud (2002) illiquidity measure (i.e., daily absolute stock return divided by US$ trading volume).

To avoid the misclassification of days with no or low trading activity (i.e., days potentially yielding a price impact of zero), we omit zero-return days from the computation of the quarterly medians.

Total Trading Costs are an estimate of the total round trip transaction costs (including bid-ask spreads, commissions, and implicit costs from shortsale constraints or taxes) based on a quarterly time-series regression of daily stock returns on the aggregate market returns (Lesmond et al., 1999).
Because the Liquidity Factor can assume negative values we add one to the raw score before computing the natural logarithm.

statistics.units: Unitless factor score before adding one and taking the natural logarithm.

review_notes: Source-first selection: the paper frames the main question as whether the liquidity effects around mandatory IFRS adoption are attributable to IFRS or concurrent reporting-enforcement changes. The principal full-sample comparison is Table 3, Eq. (2), column (6): the authors’ three-group quarterly-trend design, with bid-ask spread and the aggregate liquidity factor as parallel main outcomes. Column (7) is explicitly a sensitivity check; the later regulatory-quality, voluntary-adopter, and asynchronous-enforcement tests are follow-ups outside this selected family.

Added the required supporting fit for Total Trading Costs because that estimated measure is an input to the retained Liquidity Factor. The source describes a quarterly log-likelihood regression system but does not print its complete equation/system; the support record is flagged for review rather than reconstructed from the cited literature.
results_review_notes: Only the two frozen Table 3 column (6) baseline models are included. Other Table 3 columns, additional sensitivity tests, alternative country partitions and later tests are outside this enrichment.

The coefficients and Wald difference-test p-values are copied as printed. The p-values from the test of the IFRSEU_ENF/IFRSEU_nonENF difference are stored as separate auxiliary tests, not attached to either individual coefficient.
